question: does the I/P character representation measure motion, or threshold dither on a noisy continuous signal?
verdict: SEPARATED: change grows with lag; the delta carries motion.
notes: The SATURATED/SEPARATED predicate is the pre-registered falsifier this file was written to apply: lag-1 change above 30%, or not monotone in lag, means the delta is a dither map. It now comes out SEPARATED, so the conclusion the previous run recorded -- that the delta is dominated by threshold dither -- does NOT survive the stride fix.

That is not the same as saying the dither mechanism is gone. experiments/ascii_motion_threshold.py measures it directly on the same capture: the flip rate still falls monotonically with distance from the threshold, and 5.62% of pixels sit within +/-2 of it. What the stride fix removed was the TORN-FRAME artefact -- a large, lag-invariant change signal that was not motion at all. The residual dither is a small, structured, threshold-proximity effect sitting on top of a real motion signal, and the two are not in conflict.
consequence: None. Proceed to the labelled capture.

renderer.note: the character renderer assumes the STANDARD NV12 stride of 23,040 bytes per frame, so the capture is re-wrapped into standard NV12 first; no luma byte is changed by that re-wrap

supersedes.why: Re-measured on 2026-10-20. The previous run read the capture at W*H*3//2 = 23,040 bytes per frame; the capture on disk carries 19,200 bytes per frame, so all but every sixth frame was torn (rows 0..71 from frame k, rows 72..95 from frame k+1). The previous numbers are recorded here rather than silently overwritten.
supersedes.previous_verdict: SATURATED: the delta is dominated by threshold dither, not motion.
supersedes.verdict_changed: YES, AND IT FLIPS. The previous run read the capture at 23,040 bytes per frame, so 25 of the 30 frames were torn, and the lag curve was not even monotone: lag 1/2/3 sat at ~56-58% and lag 5 fell to 11.46%. That step is the tear signature -- every sixth frame was intact. At the correct stride the lag curve is monotone from 6.98% at lag 1 to 22.55% at lag 20, which is a motion signal, not saturation, so the conclusion this file was written to support does NOT survive.
